title: Commission adopts revised sustainability reporting standards
key_claim: On 3 July 2026 the Commission adopted revised ESRS that cut mandatory datapoints by over 60% and total datapoints by over 70%, with reporting costs expected to fall by more than 30% per company; the delegated acts go to Parliament and Council scrutiny.
frame_summary: The Commission argues that sustainability reporting under the CSRD can be made far lighter for companies while the standards still cover environmental issues including biodiversity.
verbatim_quote: reduce the number of mandatory datapoints by over 60% and the total number of datapoints by over 70%
verbatim_list: These changes are expected to reduce reporting costs by more than 30% per company

title: ISSB agrees on the proposed way forward for nature-related disclosures
key_claim: The ISSB decided to propose an IFRS Practice Statement for nature-related disclosures, with an exposure draft in October 2026. The Practice Statement would complement IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 and would have the full effect of an ISSB Standard for companies applying it; the Chair said material nature-related disclosure is not optional because IFRS S1 already requires it.
frame_summary: The ISSB argues that a Practice Statement is the least disruptive route to nature disclosure because the obligation already exists in IFRS S1 and the statement only explains how to meet it.
verbatim_quote: Applying the Practice Statement would have the full effect of an ISSB Standard for companies applying it.
verbatim_list: Providing material nature-related disclosures is not optional; IFRS S1 already requires that.

The ISSB aims to publish an exposure draft for public comment in October 2026, giving stakeholders the opportunity to provide feedback on the proposed requirements, including on whether an IFRS Practice Statement is the right form of standard-setting for nature-related disclosures.
At the same time, it provides the ISSB with a pathway to a standard-based outcome in the future.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band). Dateline is 22 April 2026 although the URL path reads /2026/05/. Quote provenance verified by hand via WebFetch.

title: Market momentum on nature accelerates as TNFD-aligned reporting doubles worldwide
key_claim: Over 1,000 organisations across 56 countries or areas have published TNFD-aligned reports, a 100% increase on 2025; average disclosure per organisation declined slightly but stayed above 8 of 14 recommended disclosures; more than 70% of survey respondents want mandatory reporting standards.
frame_summary: The TNFD argues that voluntary nature reporting has doubled in a year but that preparers and investors now want the consistency of mandatory standards.
verbatim_quote: More than 70% of survey respondents – across report preparers and investors as report users – want the certainty and consistency of mandatory reporting standards.
verbatim_list: Over 1,000 organisations across 56 countries or areas have published first-, second- or third-generation TNFD-aligned reports, a 100% increase in the number identified in 2025.
Average disclosure per organisation declined slightly but remained above 8 out of the 14 TNFD recommended disclosures.
notes: Publisher is a market-led taskforce that has said it will conclude its work once ISSB standards are finalised; it has an interest in nature reporting growing. Quote provenance verified by hand via WebFetch.

title: European Commission adopts revised ESRS
date_evidence: 23 Jul 2026 | European Commission adopts revised ESRS for sustainability reporting
key_claim: If no objection is raised, the revised ESRS are expected to enter into force on 10 November 2026 and apply mandatorily from financial year 2027, with fewer mandatory data points, new reliefs and additional exemptions.
frame_summary: EY presents the revised ESRS as a more proportionate and flexible reporting regime with lighter mandatory content and a fixed application timetable.
verbatim_quote: If no objection is raised, it is expected to enter into force on 10 November 2026 and apply mandatorily from financial year 2027.

title: Nairobi biodiversity talks set the stage for COP17 decisions
key_claim: Negotiators ahead of CBD COP17 reported continuing debates over disclosure requirements, supply-chain transparency and biodiversity impact reporting, and a global review found significant weaknesses in monitoring and reporting.
frame_summary: IPS reports that the UN biodiversity process is still arguing over whether and how companies must disclose, with finance and reporting among the weakest parts of the global framework.
verbatim_quote: Negotiations highlighted continuing debates over disclosure requirements, supply-chain transparency and biodiversity impact reporting
